statusNote.unconfirmed: Signed up on {date} but never confirmed the link in the email. That is why we don't send them campaigns.
statusNote.unsubscribed: Unsubscribed on {date} from the preference page.
statusNote.bounced: The address does not exist. Emails have been bouncing permanently since {date}.
statusNote.complained: Marked our email as spam on {date}. This cannot be undone and the address stays blocked.
statusNote.deleted: Deleted on {date}. The data has been removed.

statusAction.resubscribeNote: Only the contact can subscribe again. We will email them a link and subscribe them once they confirm it.

flagNote.snoozed: They asked for a pause until {date}. After that they come back automatically.
flagNote.anonymized: The data was erased on request on {date}. Only the record that this person existed remains.

restricted.title: This contact has restricted processing
restricted.body: {name} asked on {date} to restrict the processing of their data (GDPR article 18). Until the request is settled we must not send them anything.
restricted.consequence: In practice this means they dropped out of every segment and will not receive any campaign, even if they are in the audience.

list.title: Contacts
list.searchHint: Search ignores accents, so “novak” also finds “Novák”.
list.sortNotAvailable: This column cannot be sorted by
list.empty: No contacts yet. Import them from a file or add one manually.
list.emptyBody: A contact is one person you will email. For each of them we remember the name, the email, where they came from and what they did with your emails.
list.emptyHowTo: There are four ways to get them here:
list.emptyImportHint: Have them in Excel or in another tool? Upload the file and we will do the rest.
list.emptyFormHint: Put the form on your website and people sign up themselves.
list.filteredTip: Tip: search ignores accents, so “novak” also finds “Novák”.
list.staleCursor: That link pointed to a page that no longer exists. We are showing the first page of the same filter.
list.emptySampleHint: Fifty made-up contacts to try things on. You can remove them at any time.

selection.pageOnly: {count, plural, =0 {No contact selected} one {# contact selected on this page} other {# contacts selected on this page}}.
selection.selectAllMatching: {total, plural, =0 {Nothing to select} one {Select the # contact matching the filter} other {Select all # contacts matching the filter}}
selection.allMatching: {total, plural, =0 {No contact selected} one {# contact matching the filter selected} other {All # contacts matching the filter selected}}.
selection.selectPage: Select every contact on this page

bulk.deleteTitle: {count, plural, =0 {No contact selected} one {Delete # contact?} other {Delete # contacts?}}
bulk.deleteConsequenceLists: The contacts disappear from every list and segment.
bulk.deleteConsequenceHistory: Their open and click history is deleted.
bulk.deleteConsequenceReports: Sent campaign reports keep the counts only.
bulk.deleteConsequenceSuppression: Contacts that unsubscribed stay on the suppression list so nobody emails them again by mistake.
bulk.deleteIrreversible: This cannot be undone. We recommend an export first.
bulk.deleteExport: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing to download} one {Download this # contact as CSV} other {Download these # contacts as CSV}}
bulk.deleteExportRunning: Preparing the file. The dialog waits until it is ready to download.
bulk.deleteExportReady: The file is downloaded. You can delete the contacts now.
bulk.deleteExportFailed: The export failed, so you have no backup yet. Try it again, or delete the contacts without it.
bulk.deleteAck: I understand that deleted contacts cannot be restored
bulk.deleteAckRequired: Tick the sentence above the button. It confirms that you understand the consequence.
bulk.deleteConfirm: {count, plural, =0 {Delete nothing} one {Delete # contact} other {Delete # contacts}}
bulk.queued: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing is being deleted} one {Deleting # contact} other {Deleting # contacts}} in the background. We will let you know when it is done.

detail.addressingLocked: A person confirmed this greeting, so the tool will not overwrite it.
detail.timelineEmptyBody: Once you email {name} or they visit your website, you will see it here. It is collected automatically, you don't have to turn anything on.
detail.timelineTrackingOff: Website tracking is turned off in this project, so you only see emails here.
detail.timelineNoConsent: {name} did not consent to website tracking, so you don't see website activity here. Emails are here, they are part of the newsletter consent.
detail.timelineFilterEmpty: Nothing happened in the last {days, plural, =0 {days} one {# day} other {# days}}.
detail.readOnly: This contact is deleted, so it can only be viewed.
detail.deleteConsequenceLists: The contact disappears from every list, every segment and from the database.
detail.deleteConsequenceHistory: Their timeline and website history are deleted.
detail.deleteConsequenceReports: Sent campaign reports keep the totals only, the name and the address are gone.
detail.deleteConsequenceSuppression: The address stays on the suppression list so nobody emails it again by mistake.
detail.actionFailed: The action did not go through ({code}).
detail.confirmationResent: We sent the confirmation email again.
detail.resubscribeSent: We sent them a link. We will subscribe them once they confirm it.

consents.title: Consent history
consents.lead: Every row is evidence. A consent record cannot be edited or deleted, only new ones are added: consent you can rewrite is not evidence.
consents.subject: Contact {name}
consents.count: {count, plural, =0 {No records yet} one {# record} other {# records}}
consents.emptyBody: A record appears when someone subscribes through a form, confirms a subscription by e-mail, changes their subscription preferences, or when you write consent through the API. The history is never deleted, so whatever appears here stays.
consents.evidenceIpOff: IP addresses are not stored in this project
consents.evidenceDeclaration: The admin declared the consent is evidenced elsewhere
consents.loadFailed: The consent history could not be loaded.

vocative.title: Greeting review
vocative.lead: We are not sure how to inflect these names. Go through them by group, not by person: one decision fixes every contact with the same name.
vocative.reviewBanner: {count, plural, =0 {We know how to address every contact} one {We are not sure how to address # contact} other {We are not sure how to address # contacts}}.
vocative.groupHint: The name {name} can be either male or female. How should we address them?
vocative.savedOverride: We will remember this for future contacts named {name}.
vocative.groupCount: {count, plural, =0 {No contacts} one {# contact} other {# contacts}}
vocative.suggestedNone: We have no suggestion for how to inflect this name.

reason.genderUnknown: We cannot tell whether this is a man or a woman.
reason.genderConflict: The first name and the surname point to different genders.
reason.libraryHeuristic: We only guessed the inflection from the ending.
reason.ambiguousGivenName: The name is used for both men and women.
reason.nonLatinScript: The name is not in the Latin script, so we cannot inflect it.

vocative.deferred: The group is postponed. It stays hidden until you return it to the queue.
vocative.allDeferredBody: Nothing is left in the queue because you postponed every group. Postponing applies to this browser only.
vocative.saveOverride: Remember this for future contacts named {name}
vocative.saveOverrideHint: Without it the same name shows up in this queue after every import.
vocative.noNameHint: Contacts in this group will get the neutral “Hello”.
vocative.deferHint: The group disappears from the default view but is not lost.
vocative.saved: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing changed} one {We updated # contact} other {We updated # contacts}}.
vocative.queued: The group is large, so we will process it in the background. We will let you know when it is done.
vocative.softLimitTitle: Reviewing this by hand would take too long
vocative.softLimitBody: There {groups, plural, =0 {are no uncertain groups} one {is # uncertain group} other {are # uncertain groups}} and they cover {ratio} of your contacts. Going through them one by one makes sense for dozens, not for hundreds.
vocative.softLimitAction: Use the neutral greeting for uncertain contacts
vocative.softLimitActionHint: Recommended. Those contacts get “Hello” and the queue is cleared. You can still fix individual names later.
vocative.empty: The queue is empty, the greeting is right for every contact.
vocative.emptyBody: We know how to address every contact. After the next import only the names we are unsure about will show up here.

suppressions.title: Suppression list
suppressions.lead: We never send to these addresses. It protects you from emailing someone who does not want it or whose emails keep bouncing.
suppressions.selectPage: Select every address on this page
suppressions.complaintLocked: An address that reported spam cannot be unblocked.
suppressions.gdprLocked: The last trace of an erased person. It cannot be removed.
suppressions.bounceTooRecent: An address whose emails kept bouncing permanently can be unblocked after 30 days. {days, plural, =0 {Less than a day left} one {# day remaining} other {# days remaining}}.
suppressions.unsubscribeSelfService: It clears itself once that person subscribes again and confirms it by email. It cannot be done by hand, because coming back has to be their decision.
suppressions.removeConsequenceSend: From that moment a campaign can reach the address again.
suppressions.removeConsequenceAudit: Who removed the address and when stays in the audit log.
suppressions.removeNote: Note explaining why you remove it
suppressions.removeNoteHint: Whoever handles a future complaint will read it.
suppressions.bulkRemove: {removable, plural, =0 {None of the selected addresses can be removed} one {Remove # of {total} selected} other {Remove # of {total} selected}}
suppressions.bulkRemoveNote: {blocked, plural, =0 {Every selected address can be removed} one {# address cannot be removed, see the reasons in the table} other {# addresses cannot be removed, see the reasons in the table}}.
suppressions.revealNote: We write showing the full address to the audit log.
suppressions.empty: You have no blocked addresses yet.
suppressions.emptyBody: Addresses land here on their own when someone reports spam, unsubscribes or their email bounces for good. You can also add one manually.
suppressions.filteredBody: Try clearing the reason filter, or search for another part of the address.
suppressions.addBody: A blocked address receives no campaigns. Blocking applies to the whole project and can be undone.
suppressions.addDetail: Note on why you are blocking it
suppressions.addDetailHint: Optional. Whoever handles a complaint later will see it.
suppressions.addFailed: The address could not be blocked.

fields.title: Custom fields
fields.lead: A custom field is anything you track about contacts beyond the name and the email: city, customer number, date of the last order.
fields.label: Name
fields.usage: {used, plural, =0 {No fields out of {limit}} one {# field out of {limit}} other {# fields out of {limit}}}
fields.indexedUsage: {used, plural, =0 {No faster fields out of {limit}} one {# faster field out of {limit}} other {# faster fields out of {limit}}}
fields.usageHint: Every faster field makes imports slower to write, which is why you get fewer of them.
fields.limitReached: You cannot add another field. Archive or delete an unused one first.
fields.indexedLimitReached: You cannot speed up another field. Turn it off on a field that does not need it.
fields.archiveHint: The field disappears from the menus but the values stay and segments keep working. It is safer than deleting.
fields.deleteImpactContacts: {count, plural, =0 {No contact has a value} one {# contact has a value} other {# contacts have a value}} and the values will be lost.
fields.deleteImpactTemplates: {count, plural, =0 {No template uses the field} one {# template uses the field and will stop working} other {# templates use the field and will stop working}}.
fields.deleteImpactSegments: {count, plural, =0 {No segment refers to the field} one {# segment refers to the field and will stop counting} other {# segments refer to the field and will stop counting}}.
fields.deleteImpactForms: {count, plural, =0 {No form writes into the field} one {# form writes into the field} other {# forms write into the field}}.
fields.deleteBlockedByCampaign: The scheduled campaign {campaign} uses this field, so it cannot be deleted. Cancel the campaign, or wait until it is sent.
fields.deleteAck: I understand that the values will be lost and templates using this field will stop working
fields.empty: You have no custom fields yet.
fields.emptyBody: A custom field is an extra detail you keep about contacts: city, customer number or the date of the last order. You can then filter by it and use it inside emails.

tags.title: Tags
tags.lead: A tag is a manual label. A segment keeps itself up to date from a condition, a tag is assigned by you.
tags.name: Name
tags.contacts: {count, plural, =0 {No contacts} one {# contact} other {# contacts}}
tags.mergeBody: Contacts tagged {source} will get the tag {target} and the tag {source} will be gone.
tags.emptyBody: A tag is a manual label you sort contacts with: VIP, Brno, from the trade fair. Unlike a segment it does not update itself, you assign it.

lists.title: Lists
lists.lead: A list is a group people subscribe to. Who is in it is decided by you and by them, not by a condition.
lists.name: Name
lists.members: {count, plural, =0 {No confirmed contacts} one {# confirmed contact} other {# confirmed contacts}}
lists.pending: {count, plural, =0 {nobody waits for confirmation} one {# waits for confirmation} other {# wait for confirmation}}
lists.confirmationModeOneStepHint: The person clicks the link in the confirmation email and their subscription is confirmed. The page submits the confirmation for them, so a security scanner that merely opens the link subscribes nobody.
lists.confirmationModeTwoStep: A click and a confirmation on the page
lists.confirmationModeTwoStepHint: After clicking the link a page with a Confirm subscription button opens. It is one extra click, but you have proof that a human confirmed it.
lists.confirmationModeChanged: Saved. It applies to confirmation emails sent from now on.
lists.emptyBody: A list is a group of people who signed up for something: a newsletter, product news, event invitations. A campaign goes to a list or to a segment.

forms.title: Forms
forms.lead: Put a form on your website and people subscribe themselves. It writes into the list you pick.
forms.name: Name
forms.signups: {count, plural, =0 {No signups in 30 days} one {# signup in 30 days} other {# signups in 30 days}}
forms.doubleOptInHint: After the form is submitted we email the person a link and subscribe them once they click it.
forms.doubleOptInDisableBody: Without a confirmation email, anyone can subscribe someone else's address. This increases the risk of spam complaints and may leave you unable to prove consent. Turn it off anyway?
forms.droppedSilently: We dropped the submission silently because it looked like a bot.
forms.emptyBody: You put a form on your website and people subscribe to a list themselves, without you doing anything. It is the cleanest way to get consent, because you have proof of it.

embed.title: Putting the form on your website
embed.who: Who will put the form on the website?
embed.whoDelegate: I will send it to whoever runs our website
embed.whoDelegateHint: We prepare an email with the code and the instructions. You only fill in the address.
embed.whoHosted: I will use a ready-made page (we have no website yet)
embed.whoHostedHint: The form runs on our address, which you can link from anywhere.
embed.delegateEmail: Email of the person running the website
embed.variantScriptHint: Looks best and adapts to the page. It needs a script to be allowed on the website.
embed.variantIframeHint: For content systems where a script cannot be added.
embed.variantHtmlHint: Full control over the looks. It works without JavaScript, but it loses the bot protection.
embed.otherVariants: Cannot embed a script? We also have a frame version and a plain HTML form that works without JavaScript.
embed.testEmpty: No signup has come through this form yet.

privacy.title: Consent and privacy
privacy.consentsLead: For every purpose we record whether the consent holds, whether the person withdrew it, or whether they never gave it. Legally these are three different situations, not three shades of one.
privacy.consentCount: {granted, plural, =0 {No purpose has a valid consent} one {Consent holds for # purpose} other {Consent holds for # purposes}}.
privacy.softOptInHint: Use it only for your own customers, to whom you offer similar goods or services and who had the chance to refuse when you got their address.
privacy.requestsLead: You have one month to settle a data subject request. The deadline column is the whole point of this table.
privacy.deadline: {days, plural, =0 {the deadline is today} one {# day left} other {# days left}}
privacy.deadlineOver: {days, plural, =0 {the deadline expired today} one {the deadline expired # day ago} other {the deadline expired # days ago}}
privacy.deadlineUrgent: The deadline is within five days

gdpr.exportReady: Your data is ready to download. The link is valid for 7 days.
gdpr.eraseConfirm: Really erase all data for this contact? This cannot be undone.

privacy.eraseConsequenceData: The name, the address and all data are erased for good.
privacy.eraseConsequenceTimeline: The timeline and the behaviour history are deleted.
privacy.eraseConsequenceReports: Sent campaign reports keep the totals only, without the name and the address.
privacy.eraseConsequenceSuppression: The address stays on the suppression list so nobody imports it back by mistake.
privacy.eraseSuppressionNote: The last point is deliberate: it is the only protection against an erased person coming back with the next import.
privacy.eraseAck: I understand that the data is gone for good and only the blocked address remains

requests.empty: Nobody has filed a GDPR request yet.
requests.emptyBody: A request appears when someone clicks Download a copy of my data on the preference page, or when you file it here on their behalf. The one month deadline starts on the day it is filed.

privacy.retentionLead: Once the period is over, the data is deleted or anonymized on its own. Consent records and blocked addresses are never deleted, because they are evidence.
privacy.retentionWarnTitle: The first run deletes more than you expect
privacy.retentionWarnBody: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing will be deleted} one {The first run deletes # row} other {The first run deletes # rows}}, which is more than a tenth of the table.
privacy.retentionBelowMinimum: The shortest possible period is one day. Zero would mean deleting immediately.

inbound.title: Inbound webhooks
inbound.lead: An inbound webhook is an address your shop posts to when something happens. We turn it into a new or updated contact.
inbound.urlHint: Put this address into the webhook settings of your shop.
inbound.secretOnce: You can see the secret only now. Save it, we will not show it again.
inbound.signatureNoneWarning: Without a signature, knowing the address is enough to create a contact. Restrict at least the IP addresses you accept requests from.
inbound.mappingLead: Click a value in the request and tell us what it is. We map on a real request, not on the documentation of your shop.
inbound.mappingNoRequest: No request has arrived yet, so there is nothing to map on. Let your shop send one real order.
inbound.mappingTestResult: This is what the contact would look like. We saved nothing.
inbound.mappingReplay: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing to process} one {Process # unmapped request} other {Process # unmapped requests}}
inbound.deliveryDroppedNote: We stored the request but we don't know yet what it means.
inbound.deliveryRejectedNote: We rejected the request. The reason is in the response body.
inbound.noExternalId: The messages carry no event identifier, so we cannot tell a repeated delivery apart. Two identical orders in a row will be processed twice.
inbound.empty: You have no inbound webhook address yet.
inbound.emptyBody: An inbound webhook address can create and subscribe a contact every time somebody buys in your shop. Setting it up takes ten minutes and then it runs on its own.

unsubscribe.listScope: You are unsubscribing from {list}. You will still receive our other emails.
unsubscribe.done: Done, we will not email you again.
unsubscribe.inFlightNotice: The unsubscribe applies from now. If one more email arrives, it was sent moments ago and it will be the last one.
unsubscribe.globalScope: You are unsubscribing from everything. We will not email you again.
unsubscribe.preferencesLink: I just want to change my settings

preferences.snoozeBody: You do not have to unsubscribe. We can take a break and start again later.
preferences.exportData: Download a copy of my data
preferences.export_dataDoneBody: We will prepare a copy of your data and send it to your address.
preferences.erase_dataDoneBody: We will delete your data and send confirmation to your address.

invalidLink.title: This link is not valid
invalidLink.body: The link from the email expired or was damaged. Try opening the original message again.

confirm.title: Confirm your subscription to {list}
confirm.body: One more click and you will start receiving {list} from {sender}.
confirm.twoStepExplainer: Nothing is confirmed until you press the button. We do it this way so that an automated link checker cannot subscribe anyone.
confirm.expiredBody: The confirmation link is valid for a limited time. We will send you a new one.
confirm.doneBody: From now on we will send you {list}.
confirm.already_usedTitle: You are on the list already
confirm.already_usedBody: This link has already been used. There is nothing else to do.
confirm.expired_resentTitle: We sent you a new link
confirm.expired_resentBody: Check your inbox, the confirmation email is on its way.

reactivation.promptTitle: Do you still want our emails?
reactivation.promptBody: You have not opened anything for a while. One click confirms that you still want to hear from us.
reactivation.title: Thanks, we will keep going
reactivation.body: We noted that you still want our emails.

form.thanksTitle: We sent you an email with a link
form.thanksBody: Click the link in the email we just sent to finish subscribing.

import.detected: We detected {encoding} encoding and {delimiter} as the separator.
import.doneWithErrors: Imported {count} contacts. {errors} rows failed. Download, fix and upload them again.

contactSuppressed.title: The address is blocked
contactSuppressed.body: We don't send to this address because its owner did not want it or the emails kept bouncing. Open the suppression list to see the reason.

contactLimitReached.title: The project reached its contact limit
contactLimitReached.body: No more contacts can be added. Free up room by deleting unused ones, or raise the limit in the project settings.

subscribeBlockedComplaint.title: This person reported spam
subscribeBlockedComplaint.body: An address that reported spam cannot sign up again. It is the strongest negative signal a recipient can send, and working around it would hurt the deliverability of the whole project.

suppressionNotRemovable.title: This address cannot be removed
suppressionNotRemovable.body: The blocking reason does not allow it. For a spam complaint and for a GDPR erasure there is no way back, not even for the project owner.

suppressionTooRecent.title: It is too early to unblock
suppressionTooRecent.body: An address whose emails kept bouncing permanently can be unblocked after 30 days. Until then the email would bounce again and hurt the sender reputation.

fieldLimitReached.title: No more custom fields
fieldLimitReached.body: The project allows {limit} fields. Archive an unused one first, which frees the slot and keeps the values.

indexedFieldLimitReached.title: No more faster fields
indexedFieldLimitReached.body: Filtering can be sped up on at most {limit} fields. Each one makes imports slower to write, which is why there are few. Turn it off on a field that does not need it.

fieldTypeImmutable.title: The field type cannot be changed
fieldTypeImmutable.body: Changing the type would lose values on some contacts. Create a new field with the right type and move the values into it.

fieldUsedByScheduledCampaign.title: A scheduled campaign holds the field
fieldUsedByScheduledCampaign.body: The campaign fills the value in only while sending, so after deleting the field the email would have a blank in the middle. Cancel the campaign, or wait until it is sent.

gdprNotVerified.title: The identity of the requester is not verified
gdprNotVerified.body: Before you hand out personal data it has to be clear that its owner is asking for it. Verify the identity and then finish the request.

retentionBelowMinimum.title: The period is too short
retentionBelowMinimum.body: The shortest possible period is one day. Zero would mean deleting immediately and nothing could be reclaimed.

contactInRunningCampaign.title: The contact is in a running send
contactInRunningCampaign.body: A campaign is being sent to them right now, so they cannot be touched. Try again in a moment, or pause the send.

validationFailed.title: We couldn't submit the form
validationFailed.body: We described what needs fixing next to the fields below.

fallback.title: Something went wrong
fallback.body: The server description of the error is below this text. If it does not help, send the request number to support.

form.emailHint: The address is the key of a contact. If you already have it in this project, we will fill in the existing contact instead of creating a second one.
form.changeEmailConsequenceHistory: It stays the same contact. History, statistics and the timeline move to the new address.
form.changeEmailConsequenceConsent: List subscriptions and recorded consents are not reset. The contact therefore stays confirmed on an address nobody confirmed.
form.changeEmailConsequenceSuppression: We refuse the new address if it is blocked after a complaint or an article 17 erasure.
form.changeEmailConsequenceCollision: We also refuse it if another live contact already has it. Two contacts cannot share one address.
form.titlePrefixHint: For example Ing. or MUDr. It also hints at the gender.
form.genderHint: We inflect the greeting by gender. If you leave it out, we guess it from the name.
form.greetingPreviewEmpty: Fill in a name and we will show you how the contact gets addressed.
form.greetingUncertain: We are not sure about this name. Check the vocative before you save.
form.greetingGenderUnknown: We could not tell the gender, so we address them without inflection.
form.greetingLocked: A person confirmed this greeting. Changing the name makes us compute it again.
form.noTagsYet: This project has no tags yet.
form.newTagsHint: Separate them with commas. Tags that do not exist yet get created.
form.listsHintCreate: We add the contact as unconfirmed. You can email them once they confirm the subscription.
form.listsHintEdit: Ticking a list emails the contact a confirmation and subscribes them once they click it. Unticking unsubscribes them right away.
